title: an Animation Blueprint with a state machine and transitions
proves: author an AnimBP against a real skeleton, read the state machine back, and drive it from a pawn

steps.label: primitive puerts_find_assets is registered
1. find a Skeleton in the project to build against
1. the project contains at least one Skeleton
2. find AnimSequences the state machine can play
2. at least three AnimSequences exist to blend between
3. determine whether the slice asset needs create or patch
primitive puerts_anim_blueprint_build is registered
3. build the state machine from one spec
3. the Animation Blueprint compiled clean
primitive puerts_anim_blueprint_inspect is registered
4. read the state machine back with the independent inspector
4. all three states are in the asset
4. all four transitions are in the asset
primitive puerts_anim_blueprint_patch is registered
5. apply the same desired state through the failure-atomic patch path
5. the patched Animation Blueprint compiled clean
5. patching replaced the state machine instead of appending another
primitive puerts_blueprint_build is registered
6. attach the Animation Blueprint to a pawn's SkeletalMeshComponent
7. see the state machine blend
steps.detail: an Animation Blueprint only evaluates in a running game or in the asset editor's preview viewport. PIE is user-gated, and puerts_viewport_screenshot captures the level viewport, not an asset editor preview. The legacy anim_pose_snapshot / anim_pose_delta pair is the closest thing to a pose read-back and is behind the HTTP opt-in.
